claims.text: Molecular Dynamics simulations combined with a Monte Carlo Kawasaki exchange process can be used to study the size-dependent thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The initial material consists of as-synthesized FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The proposed simulations examine elevated-temperature or thermal-treatment conditions over varying nanoparticle sizes.
Atomic arrangement and diffusion mediate the thermal response of the nanoparticles.
Heating induces atomic diffusion and rearrangement in FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
A 5 nm FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle has 15% greater thermal stability than a 10 nm particle.
Thermal stability is measured through the onset temperature of phase transformation.
The predicted size-dependent difference is specified at 800 K.
The thermal stability of a 10 nm FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle at 800 K serves as the baseline.
The proposed method applies to nanoparticle sizes from 2 to 20 nm.
The accuracy of the prediction may depend on the selected interatomic potential and simulation time scale.

contradictions.description: Thermal stability is defined as an onset temperature, yet the comparison is described as occurring 'at 800 K.' An onset temperature normally results from a temperature scan and is not itself a property evaluated at one fixed temperature.

The hypothesis predicts a 15% increase, whereas the falsification rule uses a 5% threshold. It is unclear whether an increase between 5% and 15% confirms, weakens, or falsifies the stated quantitative prediction.
